name: Portal guide
about: What the words mean in this portal and how its parts fit: for people (the ? on every face) and for a model working here.
text:
The words this portal uses, what each means here (some differ from their everyday or industry use), and how the parts fit. Open a section, or type a word in the search box. Corrections and additions: save a copy of the library context *Portal guide* (Settings > Library) and edit it - that copy is what shows here and what a model is given.

How to name things in instructions: a screen is Face > View > Panel title (Tessa > Converse > This conversation), a field is its label in italics (*Context window (tokens)*), a choice is its label with its id in brackets (Chat turn (`chat_turn`)).

## The whole in one picture
- **Portal Server** - the owner's sovereign space: users, files, modules, tools, and the rules for who may do what. One primary user (the owner) per portal; everyone else works inside what the owner gives them.
- **Aviary** - the AI as a whole: one user of the portal, with everything AI on this portal inside its scope (pipelines, members, models, pools). *Tessa* is the name of that one entity as a person you talk to. Every AI task is a sub-user scoped inside what Aviary has been given.
- **Corvid** - where people and AI work together: the faces (Tessa, Athena, Settings, Asio, Kimi, Sunbird, Lyrebird, Parrot). It shows, asks and decides; Aviary does the work.
- **Magpie** - a program on each computer that the portal uses as its hands and informant there: it says what the computer has, what it can do and what it needs, and carries out what the portal decides (start a model, move a file, run a request).
- **Decisions flow down, information flows up**: the owner decides (or delegates to Aviary); the portal holds the overall picture; Magpie advises and enacts. A setting someone made is used as made (see *Firm*); a machine's own optimization fills only what was left open and always says what it chose.

## Users, owners and scope
The same rules for people and AI (Settings > Users and scopes; the portal core's scope.py).
- **Primary user** - an admin account: may set, change, move or remove anything, after a warning if it is risky. The final say.
- **Account** - a person or an AI with a login (*kind*: person or ai). The AI as a whole has one account (`aviary` unless set otherwise), made at install with no password anyone knows.
- **Sub-user** - `<account>/<name>`: made for one task (gone when the task or the server ends) or kept (a person's standing access through the AI in Athena). It may only do what it was granted *and* what its parent may *and* what every account it is also bound by may.
- **Thing** - `kind:path` (`pool:ingest`, `file:/data/notes`, `pipeline:chat_turn`, `machine:N2`, `tool:pause`). A grant may use `*` and covers everything under a path.
- **Acts** - see < use < edit (change without asking) < own (decide about it, remove it, grant it); each includes the ones before.
- **Grant** - an act on things given by someone who may pass it on (*may pass on*), or who owns them; optionally until a time, with a reason. A sub-user is given grants the same way by its parent.
- **Owner** - who decides about a thing. With several owners, an irreversible change needs each of them (stakes rule).
- **Check** - "May X do this?" answered with the reason, for any account or sub-user.
- **Delegation** - the primary user can grant the AI account the use of pools, the pause and stop tools, and the right to pass these on to its task sub-users; how far is the owner's choice and can be taken back at any time.
- **AI member** (library kind *agent*) - an AI that works on tasks with tools; its profile says which models and tools it uses.

## Faces (Corvid)
- **Face** - one area of Corvid with its own tab: Tessa, Chat, Designer, Athena, Kimi, Sunbird, Lyrebird, Asio, Parrot, Settings. A face has **views** (its own tabs) and each view **panels** (left, middle, right).
- **Tessa** - the portal's AI as one entity: one identity and one *stream* (its one conversation, never switched or emptied). *Collab*: on the left the *projects* - what is set before Tessa; in the middle the loaded project's tabs (each shows a chat, a run or another face's view, and may hold tabs of its own); on the right the stream, which is Tessa itself. Loading a project tells Tessa what you are working on and gives it the reach the project asks for (see it, take part, organize its chats), bounded by what its own account may. *Tessa*: who it is - its identity (account, model, how it answers, how much of its stream a turn is given, memory, LoRAs) and the values its stream answers with. *Lab*: trying the pipelines Tessa works with. *Agents*: the members it can hand work to.
- **Chat** - a plain conversation with whatever answers you choose (any chat pipeline, mode or model): the floor every user has. Changing what answers here does not change Tessa, and Tessa does not see it unless a project points at it and Tessa may.
- - **Designer** - the tools pipelines are made of and the labs built with them: *Build* (steps), *Parts* (prompts, contexts, skills, translators, kinds, faces), *Specialty* (experimental and personalized pipelines), and projects such as Workbench, each with its own views and a Design view.
- **Athena** - the same tools as others see them: everyone who is not the owner works here, inside their scope.
- **Settings** - what exists and how it is set up: machines, programs, models, pools, library, limits, members' scopes.
- **Asio** - what is happening and what happened: machines now, speeds, measurements, charts, logs.
- **Kimi, Sunbird, Lyrebird** - experts for a domain (knowledge and memory, pictures, sound and speech): specialized faces for that kind of work, using the same pipelines and machines.
- **Parrot** - the AI's way out to things outside the portal (other servers, translators, the web), and how that access is limited.
- **?** at the top of a face opens this guide.

## Pipelines, steps and runs
- **Identity** (library kind *identity*) - who an AI is over time rather than what answers one request: the account it acts as (one stream per account), its model, how it answers (a mode), how much of its stream a turn is given, its memory and LoRAs.
- **Stream** - an AI account's one conversation, with everyone who may talk with it (the grant *use* on `ai:<account>`). Each message says who it was with and which project was loaded. Someone who is not a primary user sees only their own part, and by default it recalls only that part with them. Nothing is lost from it: a message taken out is kept aside.
- **Project** (Collab) - a set of pointers (chats, runs, views of faces) with what Tessa is told about it and how far it may reach; loading it makes a sub-user `<account>/collab-<id>` for that load. Taking a project or a tab out removes only the pointer. Tessa is one. Set in Tessa > Tessa.
- **Pipeline** - a tool: a fixed chain of steps with inputs (*params*) and outputs. Built in (shipped), made by a user, or made by an AI if allowed. Owned like any other thing.
- **Step** - one part of a pipeline: ask a model (*capability* step), run a tool, call another pipeline, let an AI member work until done (*agent* step), ask a person.
- **Param** - an input a pipeline takes; shown as a field. The values a conversation sets are kept for that conversation the moment they change.
- **Mode** - a saved set of param values and roles under a name (choose it instead of setting each field).
- **Run** - one use of a pipeline, with its own record: what was given, each step, what it cost, what came out. *The run behind this* on an answer opens it.
- **Trace** - a run's steps as they happen (Tessa > Converse > *Its work now*).
- **Task left running** - a run a conversation started and checks later (`start_task` / `task_status` / `stop_task`).
- **Proposal** - a change a run or member wants to make to something shared; waits in Review until a person accepts it.
- **Schedule** - a pipeline started at set times.

## Library (what Aviary knows how to use)
- **Library** - Aviary's stored objects by kind: pipeline, prompt, context, skill, agent (AI member), mode, pool, face, schedule, translator, policy, space.
- **Shipped vs saved copy** - every kind comes with built-in items. Saving one (Settings > Library) makes your own copy, which is used instead from then on. A copy saved long ago hides later improvements of the built-in one: remove the copy to go back.
- **Prompt** - standing instructions put before the conversation.
- **Context** (library kind) - reference text a model is given while it works: a project's rules, a glossary (this guide is one). Not the same as the *context window*.
- **Skill** - instructions for doing one kind of task well, which a member can be given.
- **Translator** - how to talk to a server that does not speak Magpie's language (an Ollama, a pose bridge): its verbs mapped to HTTP calls.
- **Space** - a folder an AI member works in.

## Models, roles and placement
- **Model** - the weights file(s) a program loads (a GGUF, a folder of safetensors). Called an **asset** where it is anything a machine offers (a voice, a pose library, a knowledge base).
- **Capability** - a kind of work an asset can do: chat, generate, embed, image, speech, decide ...
- **Role** - a slot in a pipeline that needs capabilities (*answer* needs chat). A **binding** says which model fills a role, or lets placement choose.
- **Placement** - choosing the machine and model for a role when it is first used: among what can do it, what fits now, then what is fastest. A model *pinned* in the binding is used as named.
- **Plan** (a machine's answer before starting) - how it would load the model here: memory needed, where it goes (GPU / RAM), the context and KV type, how many requests at once. Verdicts: *yes* (fits now), *wait* (fits when its current work ends), *yes if* (fits if something is changed - the *ways*), *no* (does not fit by the estimate). An estimate never refuses: with nothing that fits, the nearest machine is *tried* and the run says so; only a real load failure stops it.
- **Ways** - changes that would make something fit (stop idle programs, run alone, smaller context); a person picks.
- **Choices** - the configurations the machine's own planner weighed (one per KV type), the one it would use marked.

## Machines, programs and Magpie
- **Machine (node)** - a computer running Magpie. In Settings it is a **provider** (anything that offers capabilities to the portal), named like *Magpie-N2*.
- **Program** (Magpie *module*) - something Magpie can install and run: llama (llama.cpp), colibri, image, speech, knowledge ... **Driver** - one way to install a program (vulkan, rocm, cuda, found = already on the computer). *Install again* brings its source to the newest (or a pinned ref) and builds it.
- **Server / service** - a program running: `llama:main` is the llama-server holding the current chat model.
- **Model source (remote source)** - another server a machine passes work on to (an Ollama on another computer). Its requests are shown where they run.
- **Router mode** - Magpie on a computer only to report and forward to a program there (Windows with Ollama).
- **Holding memory** - what each running program takes now. **Can be freed** - what stopping idle programs would give back.

## Context window, slots and the KV cache
- **Context window** - how many tokens one request can hold (prompt + reply). A field in a conversation (*Context window (tokens)*); empty means the machine's own plan.
- **Firm** - a value a person (or the portal) set: the machine uses exactly it and plans only the rest around it, and loads it even if its estimate says no (it says so). A value left empty is the machine's to choose.
- **Requests at once (slots, parallel)** - how many requests one model server serves together. llama splits its total window evenly: 4 at once in 16384 tokens = 4096 each. With a firm window each request gets the whole window asked for; *Requests at once on its server* sets how many (empty: 1).
- **KV cache** - the memory holding a request's context while the model works; grows with the tokens held. Its size per token depends on the model and the **KV type** (`f16` = full, `q8_0` = half, `q4_0` = about a quarter; smaller loses a little quality).
- **Cache reuse** - a new request that starts with the same text as the last one in its slot (the same instructions, the same conversation so far) reuses that part instead of reading it again: *reused* in Asio Now. **Session** - a conversation's KV cache saved to disk and loaded back when it continues on a server serving one request at once.
- **Measured vs estimated** - Magpie estimates memory before loading, measures after, and corrects later estimates (*checked against a load*).

## Pools
- **Pool** - several machines offered as one model for a kind of work (an ingestion pool across 4 nodes). A program names `pool~name` as its model; each request goes to the member that would finish it first.
- **Member / candidate** - one machine + model in a pool; it can be switched off in a pool without removing it.
- **Class** - a pool's priority: interactive, normal, background.

## Knowledge (Kimi)
- **Group** - a body of knowledge with its own models (chat for extracting, embed for searching) and its own server (LightRAG).
- **Ingest** - reading documents into a group: each piece goes to the chat model to pull out entities and relations, then to the embedding model.
- **Query** - asking a group; the answer draws on what was ingested.

## Asio words
- **Now** - per machine: the requests running there, one line each (time, tokens written, speed, the context it holds and its memory), a line for all of them together per model, and those waiting folded under their own line.
- **Working / waiting** - a request being answered / one queued for a free slot.
- **Speed** - tokens per second: *so far* while streaming (counted from what has arrived), the program's own figure once finished.
- **Path** - how fast data moves between two machines. **Memory copy rate** - how fast a machine moves data in memory (sets how fast a model can run on it).

## Same word, two meanings (watch for these)
- **context**: the *context window* (tokens a request holds) vs a library *context* (reference text given to a model).
- **model**: the weights file vs a *model* field that can also hold a pool (`pool~name`) or a source (`source/model`).
- **machine / node / provider**: the same computer seen as hardware, as a Magpie, and as something in Settings that offers capabilities.
- **run / request / job / stream**: a *run* is one use of a pipeline (many steps); each model step sends a *request* to a machine, where it is a *job*; while it answers it is a *stream* (a line in Asio Now).
- **session**: a conversation's saved KV cache on a machine - not a login session.
- **profile**: which models a pipeline uses (Aviary) - not a user profile page.
- **mode**: saved param values of a pipeline - not an operating mode of a machine (the optimizer's ON / UPPER / SET).
- **member**: an AI member (agent) vs a pool member (machine + model in a pool).
- **plan**: a machine's answer about loading vs a run's plan (the pipeline as it was started).
- **owner**: who decides about a thing vs the owner of a run (who started it).
